messages:
maria: FYI seeing ~12% P99 regression on canary after the kv-batcher refactor. Attached nsys traces (before/after). Can someone help bisect?

aj: can you paste the trace links + the commit range? also which workload / seq len dist?

maria: workload is customer-chat-sim, mostly seq len 256-512. commits: rollup from 1e2f3a -> HEAD. traces: https://perf.redwood/trace/1956789001 (baseline), https://perf.redwood/trace/1956789002 (canary). nvprof/nsys commands I used:
```
nsys profile -o before --trace=cuda,cudnn --sample=none --nvtx true --stats true -- ./run_workload --seed 42 --requests 500
nsys profile -o after  --trace=cuda,cudnn --nvtx true --stats true -- ./run_workload --seed 42 --requests 500
```

shreyas: thanks. quick glance at the timelines shows a shift in the GPU kernel mix — k_kernel_small gone, k_kernel_general invoked more often. looks like the kernel selector picks the general kernel for many batched shapes now. could be the heuristics threshold change in the batcher.

aj: also see spikes of memcpy H2D before some requests in the canary trace. that suggests KV cache eviction/rehydration happening more often. did the refactor change cache warmup or eviction policy?

maria: the refactor reduced the prefix coalescing window and added a "force-shrink" path when batcher sees >N small requests. commit id f3a9b6e changed threshold from 8 -> 4.

perf-bot: CI: nightly/perf p99 increased +11.8% vs baseline (run 1956790000) :warning:

nate: to bisect, run these steps and attach nsys timeline and kernel table. small script I use:
```bash
for c in $(git rev-list --reverse 1e2f3a..HEAD); do
  git checkout $c
  make -j && ./bench/run_fast --trace-out=trace_$c && nsys export --format=sqlite trace_$c.qdrep -o trace_$c.db
done
```
Keep request count small (~200) to keep traces comparable.

maria: ran a focused bisect overnight. narrowed to f3a9b6e which updated the batcher heuristic and the "force-shrink" branch. confirmed locally by checking two commits: parent(f3a9b6e) vs f3a9b6e. baseline shows continuous k_kernel_small usage, canary shows large number of k_kernel_general launches and H2D memcpy bursts.

shreyas: can you paste the kernel table snippet (name, launches, avg ms) from nsys? even two rows is fine.

maria: pasted excerpt:
```
Kernel Name              | Launches | Avg ms
k_kernel_small           | 432      | 0.12
k_kernel_general         | 1180     | 0.41  <-- canary more launches
memcpy_H2D               | 220      | 0.09  <-- extra warmup copies
```

shreyas: that lines up with selector fallback to general kernel which has larger occupancy and higher latency per token. hypothesis: the smaller threshold causes more batches to be considered "mixed/variable" leading selector to favor the safer general path. also eviction due to smaller coalescing window means more prefix rehydration (memcpy).

aj: sg. short-term mitigation: revert threshold change or add explicit isinstance check in selector to prefer small kernel for batched small seqs. can we do hotfix on canary?

maria: opening PR to revert the threshold to 8 and add a unit test to lock the kernel choice for shapes (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/789). will add the nsys before/after in the PR description. marking canary for rollback until fix lands. :thumbsup:

nate: optional follow-up: add an automated trace comparator that diffs kernel tables and memcpy counts during perf CI so future refactors get flagged earlier.

maria: agree — adding an issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/2145. thanks all for the fast triage.
